### Developer Edition 0.1 — reproducible personal LegeOS for the Intel/RTX 4060 reference laptop

`active` · `@legeos.milestone.developer-edition-0-1/1`

Turn the existing Ubuntu 26.04-derived LegeOS desktop and distribution control plane into a reproducible personal Developer Edition for the known Intel + RTX 4060 laptop: a declared package/image definition, narrow target-machine provisioning, Ubuntu-supported kernel/NVIDIA stable path, Rust/CUDA self-hosting, daily-driver integration, one shared file index, coherent userspace deployment rollback, and a retained known-good boot path.

### M0 — Initial project structure of the LegeOS distribution

`completed` · `@legeos.milestone.m0-initial-structure/1` · target 2026-08-17

Create the complete initial repository structure of LegeOS — a tightly integrated desktop OS on an Ubuntu 26.04 LTS core: every component home (crates, services, session, compositor integration, shell, apps, portal, CLI, installer, interfaces, distro/image/packaging, debian, tests, docs, ci), a compiling and tested Rust workspace seeded with the planning-document scaffold code (identity, associations, governor, window geometry), declarative distro configuration pinned to Ubuntu 26.04 'resolute' / kernel 7.0, ADRs for every structural decision, and this ledger.

> **Note:** Stages after M0 (planning doc 01): S1 replacement session on Lubuntu 26.04, S2 own archive + image, S3 hardware/update policy, S4 transactional deployment.

### M1 — The session runs: persistent policy, real containment, journalled files, recoverable windows, transactional host

`completed` · `@legeos.milestone.m1-session-runtime/1` · after `@legeos.milestone.m0-initial-structure/1`

Turn the M0 scaffold into working code: lege-sessiond persists every domain in the one state store and launches applications through systemd StartTransientUnit with desktop-entry import and real MIME detection; lege-resourced serves Resources1, applies protection and containment through a staged ladder with recorded traces; lege-filed runs file operations as resumable journalled transactions with trash, recents, the shared last-directory answer and search; lege-window enforces typed layers, the one-workspace invariant, explicit minimisation and recovery that works without the shell; lege-hostd runs kernel/driver updates as one resumable transaction over two boot backends with polkit enforcement. Stage 1 of planning doc 01: a replacement session, packaged, on an Ubuntu 26.04 base.

> **Note:** Scope is what the founding documents specify and what can be verified without NVIDIA hardware, a real compositor or root. Hardware validation (the test matrix), the cosmic-comp fork itself and the shell's toolkit surfaces stay for M2.

### M2 — the session runs: lege-comp on Smithay, graphical greeter and taskbar-free Home Surface

`proposed` · `@legeos.milestone.m2-session-runs/1` · after `@legeos.milestone.m1-session-runtime/1`

Make LegeOS reachable by a human. M1 finished the services but nothing drew a pixel, so there was no way to log in. M2 delivers the compositor (lege-comp, built directly on Smithay per ADR-0012 rather than forking cosmic-comp), the greeter (lege-greeter over greetd's JSON IPC, so greetd owns PAM), and a taskbar-free Home Surface on pixelkit. A bare Super tap is the primary route between windows and Home, backed by Home's window/session tiles rather than a permanent dock. The measure of done is a session a person can log into and use, including when the shell is dead: the compositor's recovery band, show-all-windows, fullscreen-escape and the fallback switcher are all reachable from compositor keybindings with no shell running at all.
